summary_en: This case uses the numerical settings of Table 8 in Chapter 8. The thermal module was run alone through sdtwin_sim.coupled to integrate three analytic cases, with the four power ports set to fixed values. The precondition requires HT-002 to have passed. The evidence file tests/results/HT-002.json records that case as passed with all 21 checks passed, and the file was written after the latest modification of the thermal module source code. The integration method was RK45 with relative tolerance 1×10^{−8}, absolute temperature tolerance 1×10^{−8} K, maximum step 10 s and output interval 1 s. The archive records these settings, and every accepted step is no longer than the maximum step within rounding error. Connections that take no part in a case were set to 1×10^{12} K/W: SR, CR, BR and DR in the single-node step case and the radiation balance case, and SR, BR and DR in the series case. In the radiation balance case JC also takes no part. Its resistance stays at 0.1 K/W, the computing node and cold plate at its two ends stay at the same temperature, and JC carries no heat: the largest measured temperature difference is 4.5×10^{−13} K and the largest heat flow is 4.5×10^{−12} W. Power ports that take no part in a case were set to 0 W. The absorptivity and emissivity of the exposed surfaces of the solar array, and of the radiator in the first two cases, were set to zero. The cold plate in the single-node step case and the radiator in the series case must hold a constant temperature, so their heat capacity was set to 1×10^{12} J/K. The assembled heat capacities, thermal resistances and exposed surface parameters agree with these inputs. Earth albedo and infrared were recorded and switched off as described in Section 9.4, and the archives of all three runs record the reason. The temperature derivatives in the archive at the initial time and at the step time were checked and agree with hand calculation from equation T3. In the single-node step case the computing node heat capacity is 500 J/K, the JC resistance is 0.1 K/W, the computing node power steps from 0 W to 300 W at 100 s, the time constant is 50 s, the integration runs to 600 s, and the integration is split at the step time. Compared with the exponential solution at the 1 s output points, at all accepted states and at times refined to a 0.05 s interval, the largest error over the run is 1.8×10^{−6} K against a criterion of 0.001 K, and the cold plate temperature changes by 1.4×10^{−7} K. In the series case the computing node heat capacity is 500 J/K, the JC resistance is 0.1 K/W, the computing node power is 300 W, the cold plate heat capacity is 1000 J/K, the CR resistance is 0.05 K/W, and the integration runs for 3000 s, about 30 of the slowest time constants; the radiator temperature changes by 8.6×10^{−7} K. The temperature difference between the computing node and the radiator is 44.99999996 K against an analytic value of 45 K, an error of 3.8×10^{−8} K against a criterion of 0.001 K. The error of the cold plate to radiator temperature difference is 2.3×10^{−8} K, and the transient differs from the two-node analytic solution by 1.2×10^{−6} K. In the radiation balance case the radiator front face has absorptivity 0.6 and area 1 m^{2}, faces the Sun under 1000 W/m^{2} of direct sunlight and absorbs a fixed 600 W. Both faces have emissivity 0.8, and the radiating area is 2 m^{2}. Throughout the run the radiator receives only this fixed input power and its own surface emission; the largest sum of absolute heat flows into the radiator through SR, CR, BR and DR is 1.1×10^{−10} W. The Stefan-Boltzmann constant is taken from Table 5 in Section 4.4 as 5.670374419×10^{−8} W·m^{−2}·K^{−4}, which equals the CODATA recommended value. The radiator was integrated from 320 K for 4000 s, about 34 linearized time constants. The steady temperature is 285.170688 K against an analytic value of 285.170688 K, with an error below 1×10^{−9} K against a criterion of 0.001 K, and the transient differs from the implicit analytic solution by 3.3×10^{−7} K. The numerical solutions of all three cases agree with the analytic solutions.
